correctness.rationale: With B having rows indexed by even vertices and columns by odd vertices, distinct columns have disjoint neighborhoods or two shared neighbors in a negative square; the latter contributions cancel. Thus B^T B=5I and, since B is square, BB^T=5I. The odd fields B^T u consequently have total square 80, giving b+3c=8 and a=8+2c. A prescribed field of magnitude five forces its five spins up to one common sign, giving 4096 assignments. A pair of such fields at distance two contradicts square parity; each distance-four pair has disjoint neighborhoods and contributes 256 assignments. There are 40 distance-four pairs and no triangle of them (distinct weight-four differences have xor weight two). Inclusion-exclusion gives 10240,45056,10240 assignments for c=0,1,2, respectively. Multiplying the independent odd-spin factors proves the entire Laurent polynomial. The highest profile score is 32-2c; flipping one unit field lowers it by two, so the first two multiplicities are 10240 and 8*10240+45056=126976. Score 32 means (80-32)/2=24 negative edges, and connectedness makes switching exactly two-to-one. Gauge completeness follows because the square moves interchange distinct consecutive coordinate flips in any closed walk; equal consecutive flips cancel, so squares generate the cycle space. The independent bounded replay python3 /workspace/replay_independent.py 5 used Gray-code field updates and a separate subset-sum calculation for every even assignment, verifying the three profiles, every score coefficient, symmetry and total mass 2^32. The proof, not just the replay, explains these counts.

value.rationale: Zero-field density of states is a natural exact invariant of the classical 32-spin fully frustrated model. The known minimum gives no entropy/degeneracy even at the ground state. This three-profile formula supplies the full thermal count and the first excitation with an exact mechanism, rather than a single arbitrary table entry. The value is for Q5 at zero field, not for higher dimensions or an orbit classification.
